correctness.rationale: Legendre endpoint Gram calculation gives a,b for each integer degree d>=1, and the exact two-block Schur inverse gives the claimed complete-bipartite vertex kernel with factor 1/q. Summing q cloned edge kernels proves the exact L-infinity evaluation norm. The triangle inequality establishes monotonicity, the reproducing identity yields the optimal positivity excursion, and a separate rational exact checker verified 4032 cases. The finite checks support but do not replace the unrestricted proof.

originality.rationale: The pointwise 1/q edge-kernel cloning identity for every integer polynomial degree d>=1, its sharp vertex-evaluation norm reduction, and all-degree monotonicity were compared by mathematical implication with general interval spline bounds, metric-graph finite-element mass-matrix methods, and known fixed-degree vertex examples. The inspected primary results do not state or entail this all-degree identity without the present block decomposition and inverse-row cancellation. residual_risks: The 2017 quantum-graph finite-element paper uses Schur complements and might include an implicit related matrix observation, although its inspected statements do not imply the all-degree endpoint result.

value.rationale: The all-degree factor-1/q kernel cloning exactly reduces vertex sensitivity on dense bipartite metric graphs to a sparse star, revealing stability invariance under blow-up, with sharp norm and positivity-defect consequences. It covers all polynomial orders at once and provides a nontrivial structural equivalence instead of an arbitrary parameter slice or routine finite enumeration.
